papers_read.title_as_printed: Predicting Progression from Mild Cognitive Impairment to Alzheimer's Disease using MRI-based Cortical Features and a Two-State Markov Model (Ficiara et al., Proc IEEE ISBI 2021; PMC author manuscript)
Multimodal multitask learning for predicting MCI to AD conversion using stacked polynomial attention network and adaptive exponential decay (Ho, Jeong, Kim; Scientific Reports (2023) 13:11243)

what_each_reports.P-198: 721 ADNI-1/2 MCI (533 sMCI, 188 converted to AD by a follow-up about 2 years later). A two-state continuous-time Markov model, followed by logistic regression on the estimated transition probabilities and rates; one cycle of stratified 10-fold CV. Baseline model WITHOUT MRI covariates: AUC 0.56 +/- 0.10, accuracy 0.65. With sulcal-width covariates: AUC 0.71 +/- 0.09, accuracy 0.72. With cortical-thickness covariates: AUC 0.78 +/- 0.08, accuracy 0.75.
what_each_reports.P-239: 676 ADNI baseline MCI (249 eMCI, 427 lMCI); clinical data plus SPM/PyRadiomics features from T1 MRI; 5-fold CV. Two tasks: (1) eMCI vs lMCI stage classification, accuracy 83.19% and AUC 0.91; (2) time-to-AD-conversion prediction, C-index 0.846 (reported as 0.85), Brier score 0.132. The AUC 0.91 belongs to the eMCI/lMCI stage task, not to conversion.

quantity_a: As recorded (0.56): ROC AUC of a 2-year MCI->AD prediction from a Markov model with no MRI covariates, i.e. a covariate-free baseline. The paper's MRI-based results are AUC 0.71 (sulcal width) and 0.78 (cortical thickness), 10-fold CV, ADNI MCI.
quantity_b: As recorded (0.91): ROC AUC of early-MCI vs late-MCI stage classification at baseline, which is not a conversion task. P-239's conversion result is a survival C-index of 0.846 for time to AD from clinical + radiomics features.
incompatible_if_same: No. The recorded figures come from a covariate-free baseline model (P-198) and from a stage-classification task (P-239), so neither is the contested MCI->AD conversion quantity. On the nearest real counterparts (P-198 cortical-thickness AUC 0.78 +/- 0.08 for 2-year conversion; P-239 conversion C-index 0.846), the metric types differ (ROC AUC vs survival C-index), and the predictor sets differ (MRI only vs clinical + radiomics).

gates.task: mismatch as recorded: P-239's 0.91 is eMCI vs lMCI stage classification, not T2 conversion.
gates.dataset_family: match: both ADNI (ADNI-1/2 MCI in P-198; ADNI baseline eMCI/lMCI from the TADPOLE data in P-239); subject overlap is likely.
gates.modality_family: mismatch: P-198's recorded 0.56 uses no imaging at all (baseline Markov model); its MRI models use FreeSurfer thickness and BrainVISA sulcal width. P-239 combines clinical data (cognitive scores, biomarkers) with MRI radiomics.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: P-198's 0.56 is a 2-year conversion ROC AUC from a no-covariate model; P-239's 0.91 is a stage-classification AUC, and its conversion metric is a survival C-index (not a ROC-AUC).
performance_validity: flag does not apply: no value >= 0.97, and neither recorded figure is a conversion-performance estimate of the kind compared.
independence: Both draw on ADNI MCI participants and very likely share subjects. Distinct author groups.
grounds: Claim_a misreads P-198: 0.56 is the AUC of the baseline Markov model with no MRI covariates; the MRI models reach 0.71 and 0.78.
Claim_b misreads P-239: 0.91 is the AUC for early vs late MCI stage classification, not for predicting MCI->AD conversion.

With both claims corrected, there is no conversion disagreement left to adjudicate: P-198's 2-year ROC AUC of 0.78 and P-239's time-to-conversion C-index of 0.846 are different metric types from different predictor sets, and neither paper disputes the other.

record_defects: claim_a 'P-198: AUC 0.56 on T2' reports the covariate-free baseline model, not P-198's MRI-based result (best AUC 0.78, cortical thickness).
claim_b 'P-239: AUC 0.91 on T2' is wrong: 0.91 is eMCI vs lMCI stage classification; P-239's conversion result is C-index 0.846.
modality_family 'structural_mri' is wrong for both recorded figures: P-198's baseline uses no MRI, and P-239's model is clinical + radiomics.
The registry's study_design_type 'survival_analysis' for P-239 fits its conversion task, but the AUC in Best_Metric comes from its classification task.
gap_magnitude 0.35 comes from two misread figures.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in the two PDFs. A candidate built on P-239's C-index 0.846 would need a survival-C-index comparator with the same predictor set, and P-198 reports none.
